data.body:
OPERATOR APPROVAL (2026-09-03, joeoakhart) — Decision A.

Removal of the eight environment/config aliases is APPROVED as a pre-1.0 breaking change:
REBAR_NO_SYNC, COMPACT_THRESHOLD, SCRATCH_BASE_DIR, REBAR_ACLI_TIMEOUT,
RECONCILER_ABSENT_GET_BUDGET, REBAR_ID_GUARD_MODE, REBAR_VERIFY_OVERLAP_ENABLED,
verify.overlap_enabled.

IMPORTANT MODIFICATION TO THE PLAN: hard-error ("fail-loud" tombstone) behavior is NOT
required. The operator's stated goal is to SIMPLIFY the codebase by removing deprecated/unused
references. There are very few clients today and none are expected to be using these variables.
Therefore the preferred migration is CLEAN REMOVAL of the alias declarations and their active
parsing/warning paths, not conversion to `_tomb`/error tombstones.

Plan must be revised accordingly before claim:
- Drop the requirement to convert each alias to an `error` tombstone; delete the alias
  declarations and their resolution/warning paths outright.
- The ADR still records the operator-approved permanent-to-removed reclassification and cites
  this approval, but its migration rationale is "removed for simplification (no expected
  clients)", not "fail-loud detection of removed input".
- Adjust Testing/AC that asserts loud-failure error messages: instead assert the old spellings
  are simply gone (no active parser/warning) and the canonical spellings retain their prior
  typed behavior, including the two transformed-value boundaries (REBAR_NO_SYNC inverse-pull,
  REBAR_ID_GUARD_MODE). The complete-population residual-reference sweep still applies.

An agent will revise the plan to match this decision and re-run plan-review before claiming.
